article:
One brain is enough

A model is a very good guesser you can talk to. It reads what you typed. It predicts what should come next. Sometimes that next thing is a paragraph. Sometimes it is a whole website. Sometimes it is a picture. The job does not change: you ask, you look, you correct.

You do not need a zoo. You need one model you will open every day, and a second tool when the first one cannot draw or cannot see.

What they can do

Write files. Rewrite files. Explain a red error in English. Turn a sentence into a first version. Look at a screenshot if you give them one. Suggest the next boring step you would rather not think about.

What they cannot do: know your bank password. Know whether the site is actually live. Care if you lose a customer. Remember last Tuesday unless you put last Tuesday in the chat. They will also invent APIs that do not exist, and sound sure while they do it.

Which one for which job

In this house the default is Grok. Code, plans, arguments, the first draft of an article, the thing that talks back when the deploy fails. Imagine when the job is a still or a clip. A smaller or cheaper model only if you are doing something repetitive and the good one is busy — not as a personality.

Do not pick a model because a thread said it is “better at React.” Pick the one whose chat you will actually return to. Switching models mid-build is how folders get haunted.

How I actually do it

Scratchbox did not need three models. It needed one that could stand in Xcode with me and not panic at Swift. Send Reorder needed one that could hold Shopify’s dull objects in its head. Parallel 51 needed a model that could make a globe feel like a toy, not a thesis.

When the job is a picture for Play, I leave the code chat and go to Imagine. Mixing those jobs in one thread makes both worse.

Where noobs get stuck

Collecting accounts. A folder of screenshots of leaderboards. Asking five models the same question and then doing none of the answers. The other freeze: waiting for the “right” model to be free instead of talking to the one that is open.

Film this

Same prompt, two tools if you must — Grok for the page, Imagine for the poster. Hold them next to each other. Say: one job, one tool. Then delete the extra tabs.

Do this before chapter 03

  • Pick a default. Write it down. Mine is Grok.
  • Give it one job today. Not five.
  • When it invents a library, ask “does this exist?” before you paste.
  • Keep Imagine for pictures. Do not ask it to host a site.

Next: talking to models — chats, files, context. How you steer without becoming a prompt collector.
